mainEntity.name: Should I build an MCP server on TypeScript SDK v1 or v2?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a new project shipping in the next few months, build on v2 with exact version pins and expect one bump when the stable release lands. For a production server today, stay on v1.x: it is the maintainers' supported production release until v2 ships stable, and it continues to receive bug fixes and security updates for at least six months afterward.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to adopt the 2026-07-28 protocol revision when I upgrade to SDK v2?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The two migrations are independent. Nothing in v2 puts a 2026-07-28 byte on the wire by default, so a hand-constructed Server or McpServer keeps speaking the 2025-era protocol. You opt in explicitly per entry point using serveStdio for stdio or createMcpHandler for HTTP.

mainEntity.name: Why do my MCP tool argument descriptions disappear from the schema?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost certainly Zod 4.0 or 4.1. Those versions lack the ~standard.jsonSchema provider, so the SDK falls back to its bundled Zod for JSON Schema conversion, and .describe() descriptions live in the authoring Zod's registry, so the fallback drops them. Upgrade to zod ^4.2.0. The fallback path also emits a one-time [mcp-sdk] console warning.

mainEntity.name: Should an MCP server use stdio or Streamable HTTP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use stdio when the host runs your server as a local child process: developer tooling, filesystem access, single-user cases. Use Streamable HTTP when it is a networked service, multi-tenant, or needs its own authorization. Transport is a wiring choice at the end of your code rather than an architecture, so supporting both from one codebase is normal.

mainEntity.name: How do I keep state across MCP tool calls without sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mint an explicit handle from a tool, such as a basket_id, and have the model pass it back as an ordinary argument on later calls. This is what HTTP APIs have always done, it composes better than hidden session state because the model can reason about the handle, and it stays visible in the Inspector while debugging. For input needed mid-call, return inputRequired(...) with a sealed requestState.

mainEntity.name: Can I write MCP tool schemas as plain JSON Schema instead of Zod?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The fromJsonSchema() helper from @modelcontextprotocol/server accepts raw JSON Schema. The default validator accepts the 2020-12 dialect only, and external $ref URIs are not dereferenced, so inline your definitions under $defs and reference them as #/$defs/Name.
